questions.prompt: When must an employer record its health and safety policy in writing?

options.A: After an accident has happened on site
options.C: Under instruction from the local authority
options.D: When employing five or more people

questions.explanation: Every employer must have a health and safety policy; an employer with five or more employees must record it in writing. The threshold does not depend on company status, an accident or a local-authority instruction.

A.text: An accident may trigger a review, but it does not create the duty to record the policy. The employee threshold applies before any accident occurs.

B.text: Company structure does not decide whether the policy must be written. The deciding fact here is the number of employees.

C.text: The recording duty comes from health and safety law, not from a discretionary instruction issued by a local authority.

D.text: Every employer must have a health and safety policy; an employer with five or more employees must record it in writing. The threshold does not depend on company status, an accident or a local-authority instruction.

questions.prompt: Which regulation requires an employer to ensure a power drill they provide an employee is suitable for use?

options.A: Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations
options.B: Current edition of the Building Regulations
options.C: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations
options.D: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations

questions.explanation: PUWER requires work equipment to be suitable for its intended use, maintained and used by appropriately trained people. A power drill is work equipment, not PPE, and neither Building Regulations nor ESQCR is the direct workplace-equipment duty.

A.text: A drill is work equipment, not personal protective equipment worn to reduce exposure to a hazard.

B.text: Building Regulations govern building work and building performance; they are not the employer's work-equipment suitability rules.

C.text: ESQCR principally governs public electricity supply safety, quality and continuity rather than an employer-provided hand tool.

D.text: PUWER requires work equipment to be suitable for its intended use, maintained and used by appropriately trained people. A power drill is work equipment, not PPE, and neither Building Regulations nor ESQCR is the direct workplace-equipment duty.

questions.prompt: In England, which listed regulations provide the specific hazardous-waste controls relevant to waste solvent adhesive?

options.C: Hazardous Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2005 (as amended)
options.D: The Health and Safety at Work Act

questions.prompt: Which legislation gives a local authority specific powers to control noise from construction work?

options.D: The Health and Safety at Work Act

questions.prompt: Once the casualty is away from the heat source, what immediate first-aid action should be taken for a hand burn?

options.B: Place a dry dressing over the wound
options.C: Cool the burn under cool or lukewarm running water for 20 minutes

questions.explanation: Cooling the burn promptly under cool or lukewarm running water for 20 minutes limits continuing tissue damage. A dressing is applied after cooling; ice, creams and dry dressings are not the first step.

A.text: The premise says the casualty is already away from the source. The next priority is removing retained heat from the tissue.

B.text: A clean covering can protect the burn after cooling, but covering it first traps heat and delays the essential treatment.

C.text: Cooling the burn promptly under cool or lukewarm running water for 20 minutes limits continuing tissue damage. A dressing is applied after cooling; ice, creams and dry dressings are not the first step.

D.text: Help may be needed for a serious burn, but prompt cooling should start immediately while further assistance is arranged.

questions.prompt: A worker has slipped, cannot safely move and may have a serious spinal injury. What immediate action should be taken?

options.A: Help them stand and walk to the site office
options.B: Call 999 or 112 and keep them still unless there is immediate danger
options.C: Place them in the recovery position even though they are conscious and breathing normally
options.D: Test the injury by moving their back and legs

questions.explanation: A suspected serious spinal injury needs emergency medical help and unnecessary movement can worsen it. Keep the casualty still and monitor them unless immediate danger or loss of airway requires movement.

A.text: Standing the casualty can move a damaged spine and worsen neurological injury. Keep them in the position found unless danger requires movement.

B.text: A suspected serious spinal injury needs emergency medical help and unnecessary movement can worsen it. Keep the casualty still and monitor them unless immediate danger or loss of airway requires movement.

C.text: The recovery position is for an unconscious person who is breathing. Rolling this conscious casualty creates avoidable spinal movement.

D.text: A first aider should not provoke movement to diagnose a spinal injury. Emergency clinicians should assess and immobilise the casualty.

questions.prompt: Who must be notified immediately when an operative sustains a back injury from carrying a load?
questions.explanation: The supervisor must be told straight away because they control the work area and accident procedures. They can arrange first aid, reporting and any changes needed to prevent a repeat.

A.text: Medical help may be arranged according to severity, but a health centre is not the person controlling the site's immediate response and records.

B.text: Legal advice is not the immediate workplace reporting route for an injury sustained during a manual-handling task.

C.text: Colleagues may help make the area safe, but notifying them does not replace reporting the incident to the responsible supervisor.

D.text: The supervisor must be told straight away because they control the work area and accident procedures. They can arrange first aid, reporting and any changes needed to prevent a repeat.

questions.prompt: What are the most common construction site pollutants of water courses and rivers?
questions.explanation: Oil from plant and silt from disturbed ground are common site pollutants that can quickly enter drains and watercourses. Both can cause serious environmental harm even in small quantities.

A.text: Cement and grout washout are harmful alkaline pollutants, but this pair omits the especially common oil and suspended-silt pathways.

B.text: Oil is a common plant and fuel pollutant, but this pair omits silt washed from exposed ground and excavations.

C.text: Silt is common, but grout is a narrower site material than the oil releases associated with fuels, storage and machinery.

D.text: Oil from plant and silt from disturbed ground are common site pollutants that can quickly enter drains and watercourses. Both can cause serious environmental harm even in small quantities.

questions.prompt: Under which listed regulations must end-of-life low-pressure sodium lamps be handled as electrical and electronic waste?

options.D: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013

B.text: EAWR prevents electrical danger in work activities and systems, not the recovery and disposal of discarded lamps.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to report asbestos immediately if it is suspected as being present?

options.B: To ensure the job is not held up

questions.explanation: Suspected asbestos must be reported immediately to stop fibres being disturbed and inhaled. The key safety aim is preventing unnecessary exposure before the material is assessed.

A.text: Finding suspected asbestos is not automatically a RIDDOR report. The immediate purpose is to stop disturbance and exposure while it is checked.

B.text: Prompt reporting may pause rather than accelerate the job; programme convenience cannot take priority over fibre exposure.

C.text: Contract penalties are commercial matters and do not explain the urgent health control required for suspected asbestos.

D.text: Suspected asbestos must be reported immediately to stop fibres being disturbed and inhaled. The key safety aim is preventing unnecessary exposure before the material is assessed.

questions.prompt: Under the site's approved risk matrix, an activity is rated high and unacceptable until further controls are added. What should happen?

options.A: Continue working and complete corrective actions within a month
options.B: Continue working and complete corrective actions within a week
options.C: Stop the activity immediately and complete set actions
options.D: Stop the activity within a week and complete set actions

questions.explanation: The stated matrix classifies the residual risk as unacceptable, so the activity must not continue until the specified controls reduce it to an acceptable level. The word high has no universal stop-work meaning without the matrix condition added here.

A.text: A one-month continuation leaves people exposed to a risk the stated matrix already classifies as unacceptable.

B.text: Reducing the delay to a week does not make continued exposure acceptable; controls must be in place before the work resumes.

C.text: The stated matrix classifies the residual risk as unacceptable, so the activity must not continue until the specified controls reduce it to an acceptable level. The word high has no universal stop-work meaning without the matrix condition added here.

D.text: Waiting a week to stop contradicts the stated immediate control required for an unacceptable residual risk.

questions.prompt: What is the most appropriate action to reduce the risk of harm to workers when damaged asbestos is encountered in a building?

options.A: Stop work, prevent access and arrange assessment by a competent asbestos specialist
options.B: Issue all workers with dust masks and safety glasses
options.C: Put barriers around it and continue work in the affected area
options.D: Cover it with sheeting and continue work

questions.explanation: Damaged suspected asbestos requires work to stop, access to be controlled and competent assessment before deciding whether it should be repaired, sealed, enclosed or removed. Immediate removal is not always the correct or safest management decision.

A.text: Damaged suspected asbestos requires work to stop, access to be controlled and competent assessment before deciding whether it should be repaired, sealed, enclosed or removed. Immediate removal is not always the correct or safest management decision.

B.text: Ordinary dust masks and eye protection do not make uncontrolled asbestos disturbance safe or determine whether licensed work is required.

C.text: Barriers can help control access, but continuing in the affected area before assessment can still disturb fibres.

D.text: Improvised covering can disturb damaged material and is not a substitute for a planned repair, enclosure or removal by competent people.

questions.prompt: What item of PPE must be used when drilling a hole in a steel wall bracket using a pillar drill?
questions.explanation: Eye protection guards against ejected swarf and fragments. Gloves can catch in rotating machinery, while a hard hat and safety boots do not control the immediate eye hazard from drilling.

A.text: A hard hat protects against falling or striking objects, not swarf projected toward the operator's eyes.

B.text: Gloves can be caught by rotating machinery and do not replace eye protection against metal chips.

C.text: Safety footwear protects feet from dropped workpieces but does not control the immediate flying-particle hazard.

D.text: Eye protection guards against ejected swarf and fragments. Gloves can catch in rotating machinery, while a hard hat and safety boots do not control the immediate eye hazard from drilling.

questions.prompt: What should determine the first-aid provision for a construction site?

options.D: A needs assessment covering the hazards, workforce and likely injuries

questions.explanation: HSE requires an employer to assess first-aid needs using the work hazards, likely injuries, workforce, work patterns and site circumstances. Distance from emergency medical services can also matter, so the original single-factor wording was ambiguous.

A.text: Worker competence can affect risk, but it is only one consideration and cannot define all equipment, facilities and cover required.

B.text: Remoteness from medical help is relevant, but using it alone ignores the site's hazards, workforce and likely injuries.

C.text: The number of first aiders is an outcome of the needs assessment, not the sole input used to determine provision.

D.text: HSE requires an employer to assess first-aid needs using the work hazards, likely injuries, workforce, work patterns and site circumstances. Distance from emergency medical services can also matter, so the original single-factor wording was ambiguous.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to replace first aid supplies each time they are used?

options.C: To ensure accidents can be effectively prevented
options.D: To ensure resources are always available in case of accidents

questions.explanation: Used first-aid supplies must be replaced so treatment is available for the next incident. An incomplete kit can delay basic care when an accident occurs.

A.text: COSHH concerns exposure to hazardous substances; it does not explain restocking ordinary first-aid materials after use.

B.text: RIDDOR governs reporting specified events and does not set the contents or replenishment cycle of the first-aid kit.

C.text: First-aid supplies treat injury after an incident; merely stocking them does not prevent the accident itself.

D.text: Used first-aid supplies must be replaced so treatment is available for the next incident. An incomplete kit can delay basic care when an accident occurs.

questions.prompt: Which listed industry training scheme is a commonly recognised way to demonstrate training for erecting mobile access towers?
questions.explanation: PASMA is an industry-recognised tower-training scheme and is one accepted way to help demonstrate competence. Competence ultimately means sufficient skills, knowledge and experience; the law does not make one certificate the exclusive route.

B.text: ESQCR regulates electricity networks and supply quality; it does not train tower assemblers.

C.text: HSWA is the framework workplace-safety Act, not an industry course demonstrating tower-erection training.

D.text: PASMA is an industry-recognised tower-training scheme and is one accepted way to help demonstrate competence. Competence ultimately means sufficient skills, knowledge and experience; the law does not make one certificate the exclusive route.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk to an electrician when safe isolation is not carried out on a live circuit being worked on?

options.A: Electric shock caused by direct contact
options.B: Electric shock caused by static discharge
options.C: Electrical shock caused by electromagnetic interference
options.D: Electrical shock caused by indirect contact

questions.explanation: Without safe isolation, the electrician may touch live parts directly. Direct contact with live conductors is the immediate electric shock hazard.

A.text: Without safe isolation, the electrician may touch live parts directly. Direct contact with live conductors is the immediate electric shock hazard.

B.text: Static charge is a different phenomenon and is not the principal danger from touching an energised circuit conductor.

C.text: Electromagnetic interference can disrupt equipment but is not the shock mechanism created by exposed live parts.

D.text: Indirect contact is the older term for touching exposed metal made live by a fault; this task presents direct access to normally live parts.

questions.prompt: What type of hazardous substance is classified by the label shown in the image?
questions.explanation: The flame-over-circle hazard symbol identifies an oxidising substance. Oxidisers can intensify fire because they release or support oxygen in a reaction.

questions.prompt: What term describes loud noise itself as a source with the potential to cause hearing damage?
questions.explanation: The source with potential to cause harm is the hazard. Risk is the likelihood and severity of harm after considering exposure and controls, so the original use of potential exposure blurred the two terms.

A.text: The source with potential to cause harm is the hazard. Risk is the likelihood and severity of harm after considering exposure and controls, so the original use of potential exposure blurred the two terms.

B.text: Risk combines the likelihood and severity of harm after exposure and controls; it is not the harmful source itself.

C.text: An accident is an event, whereas the question asks for the pre-existing source capable of causing harm.

D.text: Occurrence is a generic event description and does not identify the health and safety concept of a source of harm.

questions.prompt: What is the specific hazard when cables are run in thermal insulation?
questions.explanation: Thermal insulation prevents heat from escaping from cables, so the cable can run hotter than designed. Excess heat can damage insulation and create a fire risk.

A.text: A person could be burned by a later fire, but the installation hazard is cable overheating and ignition rather than direct contact with heat.

B.text: Thermal insulation reduces heat dissipation and current capacity; it does not by itself expose live conductors to create shock.

C.text: Ordinary insulated cable overheating is an ignition risk, not normally an explosive-energy mechanism.

D.text: Thermal insulation prevents heat from escaping from cables, so the cable can run hotter than designed. Excess heat can damage insulation and create a fire risk.

questions.prompt: What term describes working from a ladder as a source with the potential to cause a fall?
questions.explanation: Working from the ladder creates a fall hazard. The risk is the likelihood and consequence of a fall after height, duration, surface, user competence and controls are considered.

A.text: Working from the ladder creates a fall hazard. The risk is the likelihood and consequence of a fall after height, duration, surface, user competence and controls are considered.

B.text: Risk is the assessed likelihood and consequence of falling after the height, task and controls are considered.

C.text: An accident is the harmful event after control has failed, not the work-at-height condition that can cause it.

D.text: An incident is an event or near miss; simply working from the ladder is the existing hazard.

questions.prompt: What practice is employed to address the potential hazard of electrical shock from trailing leads for power tools on construction sites?

options.A: Use of 110 V centre tapped supplies
options.B: Use of 230 V single phase supplies
options.C: Use of 400 V three phase supplies
options.D: Use of 500 V DC single phase supplies

questions.explanation: A 110 V centre-tapped supply limits the voltage to earth to about 55 V on each conductor. That reduces the severity of shock from damaged trailing leads on construction sites.

A.text: A 110 V centre-tapped supply limits the voltage to earth to about 55 V on each conductor. That reduces the severity of shock from damaged trailing leads on construction sites.

B.text: A 230 V conductor can place the full nominal voltage to earth, so damaged site leads present a much greater shock voltage.

C.text: A 400 V three-phase supply is intended for suitable larger loads and does not provide reduced-low-voltage protection for hand tools.

D.text: A 500 V DC supply is neither reduced low voltage nor the standard centre-tapped site-tool arrangement.

questions.prompt: Which listed extinguisher is generally preferred indoors for energised electrical equipment because it is non-conductive and leaves no residue?
questions.explanation: CO₂ is non-conductive and leaves no damaging powder residue, making it the usual listed choice for energised electrical equipment indoors. Power should be isolated if safe, and nobody should fight a fire that is spreading or blocks escape.

B.text: Dry powder can work electrically, but it obscures vision, contaminates equipment and creates a difficult indoor clean-up.

C.text: An ordinary water extinguisher can conduct current and is intended mainly for Class A solid-material fires, not energised equipment.

D.text: Wet chemical extinguishers are designed mainly for high-temperature cooking-oil fires and introduce a liquid agent around electricity.

options.B: Remove the affected area and place in bags

questions.prompt: A typical insulator for an overhead line transmission system would be:
questions.explanation: Glass and porcelain have high electrical resistance and withstand outdoor weathering. That makes them suitable insulators for overhead line supports.
